issue.title: A successful connect leads to immediate disconnection

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
If this title sounds familiar, it's because it's nearly the same title as NETTY-211. I commented on that old bug but got no love so I am creating a new issue here.

I am seeing exactly the same symptoms as NETTY-211 on Netty 3.2.7 Final. Here's a series of printlns I inserted into the code:

2012-01-10 19:38:24,125 [stdout] flirt INFO: CONNECTING SOCKET [id: 0x2804f2ec]
2012-01-10 19:38:24,125 [stdout] flirt INFO: processSelectedKeys - connecting: [id: 0x686fdca5]
2012-01-10 19:38:24,125 [stdout] flirt INFO: connect succeeds: [id: 0x686fdca5]
2012-01-10 19:38:24,125 [stdout] flirt INFO: timeout closes: [id: 0x686fdca5]

The "timeout closes" println comes from the processConnectTimeout() function that is coming along and noticing that one of the selection keys has been canceled and calling close(). Unfortunately the key that was most recently canceled was the one that was just successfully connected! This only happens when you both successfully connect AND call processConnectTimeout() in the same loop iteration.

That's what I am seeing. The code seems to indicate that that would happen. Removing a key from a selectedKeys iterator does not remove the key from the keys set, so it is picked up and closed immediately. Please let me know if you agree. This is NioClientSocketPiplineSink.java.

My fix which I have been running for a couple of days was just to delete to call to k.close() in processConnectTimeout() for all invalid keys it encounters. The end result is I am no longer getting a bunch of ClosedChannelExceptions with a stack trace that contains processConnectTimeout in it.
